items.claim: The span 9:1-9:3 is a sound unit and both edges stand, but two readings carry a witness tier. The rationale says the repeated year formula of 9:2 is texture and opens nothing under an EXTRACTED tag, while the device notes give the same reading as INFERRED; the witness holds the formula, and the device inventory holds it as a dateline entry at 9:2, but neither holds its status as texture. The device notes also call 9:1-9:3 first-person narrative under an EXTRACTED tag: 9:1 has no first-person form (the first is at 9:2), and the genre word is a reading.
items.both_sides: No cut is proposed. Onset 8:27/9:1: 8:27 closes the earlier vision on the seer's incomprehension and a PE follows it (one witness); 9:1 is a regnal dateline, one of the inventory's dateline entries. Close 9:3/9:4: 9:3 names the intended prayer and fast; 9:4 reports the praying, introduces speech and carries the book's single great-and-awesome address formula. The first-person verb chain runs across the edge, which the row states. Medium is a fair grade for one firm edge and one edge with evidence on each side.

suggested_fix.fact: The status of the 9:2 year formula as resumptive texture is a reading (INFERRED) in the rationale as it already is in the device notes; the first-person voice begins at 9:2, and the genre word is the row's reading, so only the presence of the first-person pronoun at 9:2 is a witness fact.
suggested_fix.verse: Dan 9:2 (with 9:1 for the absence of a first-person form)

evidence: MEASURED by my script over the device inventory: the datelines list holds Dan.9.1 and Dan.9.2 (8 entries in the book); i_daniel_heb at Dan.9.2; yhwh_name_heb at Dan.9.2; set_face_heb at Dan.9.3; great_and_awesome_god_heb at Dan.9.4 only. Every signal the row lists is in the inventory and none in 9:1-9:3 is omitted.
MEASURED over the mark layer (WLC/OSHB, one witness): PE after Dan.8.27; no mark after 9:1, 9:2 or 9:3; no ketiv/qere note and no paseq in 9:1-9:3.
oshb:Dan.9.2 אֲנִי֙ דָּֽנִיֵּ֔אל (OSHB/WLC) is the first first-person form of the chapter; oshb:Dan.9.1 is the dateline with a relative clause about Darius and has none.

Finding 1 (gravest, tier): boundary_rationale tags the statement that the 9:2 formula is texture and opens nothing as EXTRACTED; device_notes tags the same reading INFERRED. The two fields disagree and the weaker tag is the true one.
Finding 2 (tier): device_notes tags the statement that 9:1-9:3 are first-person narrative as EXTRACTED; the genre word is a reading and 9:1 holds no first-person form.

Form check: unit_type narrative fits the first-person framing of a unit in the vision series. The rejected merge with the prayer (9:1-9:19, 19 verses) is the strongest rival and is the right one to name.

All WEB quotations in the row are verbatim at their cited verses and every Hebrew run is a substring of its cited OSHB line (MEASURED by my script: 72 Hebrew runs and 28 WEB quotations across the five rows, none missing); no unquoted run of five WEB words was found.

items.claim: The cut at 9:14/9:15 is defensible and the grade medium_low is honest, but the sentence that justifies the 11-verse span says 9:4-9:14 has no internal formula, mark or dateline under an EXTRACTED tag. The device inventory holds a formula inside the span at 9:7 (the ascription of righteousness to the Lord), which the row itself lists among its signals and quotes; and the statement that the span is one uninterrupted speech act, the confession, under the same tag is a reading, since the quoted speech that opens at 9:4 runs unbroken to 9:19.
items.both_sides: No cut is proposed. Onset 9:3/9:4: narrated preparation behind, speech introduction and address formula in front. Close 9:14/9:15: 9:14 ends the retrospect on the refrain of not obeying; 9:15 opens with וְעַתָּ֣ה (oshb:Dan.9.15, OSHB/WLC), the adverb that conventionally turns a Hebrew prayer from review to request, and the same word recurs at 9:17. Against the edge, 9:15 still recalls the exodus and still confesses, and the first request stands at 9:16. Evidence stands on both sides but is soft on the far side, so medium_low is right.

suggested_fix.fact: Inside 9:4-9:14 the inventory records one formula, the ascription of righteousness at 9:7, and it does not open a unit; no mark and no dateline stand in the span. That the span is the confession part of a prayer running 9:4-9:19 is a reading (INFERRED), not a witness fact.
suggested_fix.verse: Dan 9:7 (formula) and Dan 9:4-9:19 (extent of the speech)

evidence: MEASURED over the device inventory: to_you_lord_righteousness_heb at Dan.9.7 (1 verse in the book), listed under formulae; great_and_awesome_god_heb at Dan.9.4; yhwh_name_heb at Dan.9.4, 9.8, 9.10, 9.13, 9.14; month_or_day_word_not_a_date at Dan.9.7. The row's signal list matches the inventory exactly.

MEASURED over the mark layer (one witness): ketiv/qere notes at Dan.9.5 (1 note) and Dan.9.12 (1 note) and nowhere else in 9:4-9:14; paseq once at Dan.9.12 and once at Dan.9.13; no parashah mark after any verse of 9:4-9:14. The row's disclosures are complete in both directions.
Finding 1 (gravest): the EXTRACTED statement that the span has no internal formula is contradicted, for the word formula, by the inventory entry at 9:7 and by the row's own signal list.

Finding 2 (tier): the statement that the span is one uninterrupted speech act shares that EXTRACTED tag; the device notes give the same statement as INFERRED, which is the true tier. The allowance for a row above nine verses is claimed for a part of a speech act, not a whole one; the row discloses the whole-prayer rival, so this is a wording and tier point and not a ground to move the cut.
Form check: unit_type doxology_or_prayer is right. The whole prayer 9:4-9:19 as one 16-verse row is the strongest rival and is the one named.
web:Dan.9.11 and web:Dan.9.13 both name the law of Moses, and 9:11 names the curse and the oath, supporting the row's summary of 9:11-9:13 (EXTRACTED from the WEB witness).

All WEB quotations in the row are verbatim at their cited verses and every Hebrew run is a substring of its cited OSHB line (MEASURED by my script: 72 Hebrew runs and 28 WEB quotations across the five rows, none missing); no unquoted run of five WEB words was found.

items.claim: The span 9:15-9:19 holds one movement, the petition with its transitional verse, and both edges fall where the form turns: at 9:15 on the adverb of transition after the retrospect closes in 9:14, and at 9:19/9:20 where quoted prayer ends in stacked imperatives and first-person narration resumes. Medium_low matches two soft edges that each have evidence on both sides and no mark.
items.both_sides: No cut is proposed. Onset 9:14/9:15: weighed under the neighbouring row; the turn word stands at 9:15 and again at 9:17, and requests begin at 9:16. Close 9:19/9:20: 9:19 ends the address in second-person imperatives and a motive clause on the divine name; 9:20 is a circumstantial clause in the narrator's voice that names the praying as still going on, so it binds forward and backward. The row states that softness.
evidence: MEASURED over the mark layer (one witness): ketiv/qere note at Dan.9.18 (1 note) only; paseq at Dan.9.15, 9.17, 9.18 (twice), 9.19 (twice); no parashah mark after any verse of 9:15-9:19. Row disclosures match in both directions.
MEASURED over the device inventory: month_or_day_word_not_a_date at Dan.9.15; no other entry falls in 9:15-9:19. Matches the row.
oshb:Dan.9.15 opens וְעַתָּ֣ה and oshb:Dan.9.17 opens וְעַתָּ֣ה (OSHB/WLC): the same turn word twice, which supports naming 9:16/9:17 as the rejected rival.
web:Dan.9.16 holds the first request (anger to be turned from Jerusalem), so the row's reason against opening the petition at 9:17 is true of the text (EXTRACTED from the WEB witness).
Observation, not a defect: 9:15 closes on confession (web:Dan.9.15 ends with two verbs of sinning), so the literature label petition holds from 9:16; the rationale already says so.

items.claim: The span 9:20-9:23 and its type are defensible, but two statements about the speech verb of 9:22 put a decision under a witness tier: the rationale says the verb of saying is a weak connective and is not used as an onset, under EXTRACTED tags, and the device notes say it opens no unit, under an EXTRACTED tag. The witness and the inventory hold the verb at 9:22; that it opens no unit is the row's decision.
items.both_sides: No cut is proposed. Onset 9:19/9:20: prayer ends behind; in front, two circumstantial while-clauses (9:20, 9:21) resume narration and bring in the messenger. Close 9:23/9:24: 9:23 ends on a paired charge to understand, וּבִין֙ בַּדָּבָ֔ר וְהָבֵ֖ן בַּמַּרְאֶֽה (oshb:Dan.9.23, OSHB/WLC), which points forward; 9:24 begins without a conjunction on a fronted numeral phrase with a new subject. Against the edge: one speaker and one addressee continue across it, no formula and no mark stand there, and 9:25 opens with a second charge of the same kind (וְתֵדַ֨ע וְתַשְׂכֵּ֜ל, oshb:Dan.9.25, OSHB/WLC), so the charge of 9:23 can also be read as heading what follows. The evidence is real on both sides and soft; medium_low is right.

suggested_fix.fact: The verb of saying stands in 9:22 after the two narrated verbs, so the messenger's speech begins inside the verse; that it does not open a unit is a reading (INFERRED). It follows that no verse-level cut separates the narration from the speech, which bears on the 9:21/9:22 rival.

evidence: MEASURED over the device inventory: yhwh_name_heb at Dan.9.20; i_saw_heb and vision_noun_hazon_heb at Dan.9.21; and_he_said_heb at Dan.9.22 (17 verses in the book); vision_noun_mareh_heb at Dan.9.23. Row signal list matches exactly.
MEASURED over the mark layer (one witness): no ketiv/qere note, no paseq and no parashah mark in or after 9:20-9:23; none after 9:19. The row's absence statements hold.
oshb:Dan.9.22 has וַיֹּאמַ֕ר (OSHB/WLC) as its fourth word, after the two narrated verbs; the speech starts mid-verse.
Finding 1 (gravest, tier): EXTRACTED covers the presence of the verb, not the judgement that it is no onset; the statement appears in boundary_rationale and in device_notes.

Form check on unit_type: narrative is acceptable for an arrival frame, and the row's category note discloses that the second half of 9:22 and all of 9:23 are speech. The tension is real: the neighbouring row and the book plan's description of this parent count the speech as running from 9:22 to 9:27, so this row holds the first two verses of a heavenly speech under a narrative label. The category note is tiered INFERRED, which is true.

Form check on the rival: of the two rejected alternatives the merge of 9:20-9:27 (8 verses, inside the target size) is the stronger, because it needs no cut inside a speech; the row lists it second and answers it briefly. Both are named, so this is an ordering point for the end review, not a defect.

items.claim: The span 9:24-9:27 is one movement, the revealed content of the messenger's speech, and it is rightly left uncut: nothing inside it marks a division from both sides. Its close is the firmest edge in the chapter (the speech ends at 9:27, a PE follows, and 10:1 is a dateline), and its onset at 9:23/9:24 is unmarked and soft, which the row says and grades as medium_low.
items.both_sides: No cut is proposed. Onset 9:23/9:24: weighed under the neighbouring row; evidence on both sides, soft. Close 9:27/10:1: the direct speech ends at 9:27 and the next verse speaks of Daniel in the third person; a PE follows 9:27 in the one witness, and 10:1 is a regnal dateline in the inventory. Interior 9:24/9:25: 9:25 opens with a charge to know, but 9:24 gives no closing signal, so the rival fails on its near side, as the row says.
evidence: MEASURED over the mark layer (one witness): PE after Dan.9.27; no mark after 9:24, 9:25 or 9:26; ketiv/qere at Dan.9.24 with 2 notes and nowhere else in the span; paseq once at Dan.9.24 and once at Dan.9.27. Row disclosures match in both directions.
MEASURED over the device inventory: vision_noun_hazon_heb at Dan.9.24; year_word_but_not_a_dateline at Dan.9.25 and Dan.9.26; dateline at Dan.10.1. Row signal list matches exactly.
oshb:Dan.9.25 opens וְתֵדַ֨ע וְתַשְׂכֵּ֜ל (OSHB/WLC), the charge that the row quotes from web:Dan.9.25 in four words with its reference.
unit_type heavenly_discourse is the book plan's own type for revelation spoken by a heavenly figure and fits.
The divided readings of 9:24-9:27 are reported neutrally with a REPORTED tag and move no edge.

Minor, not raised to a challenge: in strongest_rejected_alternative the bracket after the 9:25 quotation names the WEB layer and INFERRED but gives no tier word for the quotation itself, where the row elsewhere writes EXTRACTED with both witnesses; the quotation is verbatim and carries its reference, so nothing false is asserted.
Minor wording: the rationale calls the unmarked onset one-sided in strength while giving evidence from both sides; the grade is not affected.

unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: The 9:23/9:24 edge falls inside one speech by one speaker with no formula and no mark; it is the softest edge in the cluster and both rows at it are already graded medium_low. I support the cut as defensible, not as settled.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether the prayer is better held as one 16-verse row 9:4-9:19.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: The turn word at 9:15 is a conventional signal but 9:15 still confesses; the size allowance for a long row was written for a whole speech act, and here it is claimed for the first part of one.
